core_obligations: Choose representatives (proof lines 3877-3890): the author uses the existence of K-flat resolutions with flat terms to replace K^bullet and M^bullet so that both paths around the diagram can be computed by naive pullbacks and tensor products.

Compare the two paths (proof lines 3890-3905): with those representatives the two composites are computed by the same total complex, so the diagram commutes, since pullback and tensor product are compatible at the level of complexes with flat terms.
Conclude (proof lines 3905-3910): the commutativity for arbitrary complexes follows because the chosen representatives compute the derived functors appearing in the diagram.
proof_roadmap: Replace the two complexes by K-flat resolutions with flat terms.
Compute both composites in the diagram using the naive pullback and tensor product.
Recognise the same total complex on both paths, which gives commutativity.
Conclude for arbitrary complexes from the choice of representatives.
difficulty_reason: The lemma asserts the commutativity of a square of derived functors: pulling back the derived tensor product agrees with the derived tensor product of the pullbacks (statement lines 3848-3875, whose displayed Xy-pic diagram is delivered verbatim). The proof uses the existence of K-flat resolutions with flat terms to reduce the comparison to complexes on which both the pullback and the tensor product are computed naively (proof lines 3877-3890), where the two paths give the same total complex, and then transfers the conclusion to arbitrary complexes because the chosen representatives compute the derived functors (proof lines 3890-3910). The non-formal content is the choice of representatives that makes both paths computable. The claim is H2: one representative choice plus one comparison of total complexes.
